messages:
anya: heads-up — ran a few nsys profiles on the 2.1.4-serving branch and seeing weird timestamp drift in CUPTI events. plant: kernel-selection heuristic picks wrong path when adjacent kernel gaps look like cold starts

sam: ugh. what driver/nsys versions?

anya: nsys 2023.5.1, CUPTI provided by driver 535.104, docker image uses CUDA 12.1 runtime. trace looks like this (snippet):
```
KERNEL conv_fwd  start=1000012345 end=1000015420
KERNEL reorder  start=1000015425 end=1000015430
KERNEL quant_pack start=999998000  end=999999500  <-- timestamp jumps backwards
KERNEL conv_fwd  start=1000015440 end=1000018000
```

anya: see the timestamp drop (~3.5s) in the middle. that makes our batching heuristic think there was a big idle gap, so it flushes batch and selects a smaller kernel variant for the next request. end result: 15% perf regression on tail latency for some prompts.

lia: that looks like epoch/timestamp counter wrap or CUPTI activity buffer reorder. did you capture both OS and device timelines?

anya: yes — capture flags: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,cupti,osrt --output=run1`. OS timeline is monotonic, device events have the jump.

devin: I've seen driver versions where the CUPTI timestamp uses a different clock domain and on a context switch the value is adjusted. also some nsys builds post-2023 switched to using device timestamp epoch vs host. maybe nsys is applying a timestamp translation that mis-detects epochs.

sam: can you paste the full nsys command and the env? maybe we can force host timestamps to avoid translation.

anya: command and env: `NSYS_NVTX_PROFILER=1 NSYS_CUPTI_CHANNEL=all nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cupti,cuda,osrt -o /tmp/trace nsys_run.sh`

tracing-bot: nsys run completed: /tmp/trace.qdstrm (size 42MB) :white_check_mark:

lia: try `export NSYS_CUPTI_TIMESTAMP=host` (or analogous env; depends on nsys build) and re-run. if the driver reports different epoch we should avoid using device-only timestamps for ordering.

devin: workaround we used in staging: ignore CUPTI monotonic decreases when gap < 10ms and rebase to previous timeline. patch: `if (ts_next < ts_prev && ts_prev - ts_next < 1e7) ts_next = ts_prev + 1;` — hacky but kills false gaps.

sam: i'd rather detect the condition properly. can we repro with a minimal workload and collect `cuptiActivityEnable(CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL)` raw output? then file a bug with NVIDIA if driver mis-epochs events.

anya: going to run minimal repro with `cudaLaunchKernel` loop + sleep to reproduce drift. will push traces to /mnt/traces and tag in this thread.

lia: also add `nvprof` or `perfetto` capture if possible. nvprof uses different CUPTI path and may not show the same drift. useful cross-check.

devin: cc @sam if we want to roll a short-term change in kernel selection: make heuristic robust to small negative deltas and prefer last good kernel variant unless absolute time gap > 5ms. that reduces SLO risk.

sam: agree. let's do quick revert-safe change in serving: add 1-line clamp and flag gated by `RELEASE_EXPEDITE` so we can roll back if it hides a real gap. create PR and tag this thread.

anya: PR #4023 created with clamp + debug logging. attaching two traces: run1.nsys (orig) and run1-hostts.nsys (with host ts) in /mnt/traces/1855239876/ — will post links once uploaded.

tracing-bot: upload complete: https://s3.internal.redwood/traces/1855239876/run1.nsys

sam: great. once we have the repro i'll open an NVIDIA support ticket + include timestamps and driver version. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
